chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hajjal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:

I entered the bathhouse with Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O 'Abd al-Rahman, get waxed.' I said: 'I only got waxed a few days ago.' He said: 'Get waxed, for it is a cleansing (tahur).'

key_terms.اطَّلِ: Imperative verb meaning 'get waxed' or 'remove hair'
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: The bathhouse, a place for ritual washing and hair removal
key_terms.طَهُورٌ: A cleansing agent or source of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Is the bathhouse considered ritually pure for removing hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the ritual purity (tahur) of the bathhouse environment and its water, specifically regarding the removal of hair via lime paste (noura). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages frequent hair removal, linking physical grooming with spiritual cleanliness, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition of fitrah. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that common bathing practices contribute to the state of minor ritual purity required for prayer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Hajjal, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘I entered the bathhouse along with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abdul Rahman! Get waxing done’. So I said, ‘But rather I waxed a few days ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Get waxing done for it is a cleansing’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajj al from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “

Once I went to a bathhouse with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘O ‘Abd al- Rahman, you should apply lime.’ I said, ‘I had applied sometimes ago.’ He (the Imam) said, ’Apply it again; it is cleansing.’”
